_comment: F1 golden fixtures for the new pure export lib/checkout-reservation.ts#computeEarlyBirdRemaining(poolSize, soldCount) — a GENERIC pool-remainder calculator, deliberately not named 'tranche' in its parameters so the same function serves any 'N of X left' display. Message 6 (2026-10-07) removed this function's originally-intended consumer (Symposium/WOSA's 10-ticket tranche, dropped entirely — see F1 figures golden). Team-lead's second-pass correction gives it TWO real, live consumers within this mission: (1) F4's shared 500-ticket admission early-bird pool (weekend-pass-early-bird + the day-visitor early-bird slug, combined, poolSize=500) and (2) F6's per-event conference-seats-remaining data (poolSize=80, one call per saoc-symposium/wosa-conference). Both are real DATA consumers (F6's TicketCardViewModel.scarcity); NEITHER gets a styled visual component in this mission — that is F7, blocked on the NOS design handoff. Must read 'real sold plus active-reserved counts' (soldCount here is the caller's getSoldCountsByTicketType()-equivalent result, which already aggregates reserved+paid with lazy expiry) and never go negative, never be faked.

cases.name: exactly sold out of the tranche
oversold past the tranche (still selling at regular status, capacity 80 not yet hit) — must clamp at 0, never negative
no tranche tracked for this product (e.g. a product with no early-bird concept) — passthrough null, not 0
tranche unset (undefined) behaves identically to null

purityRequirement: The function must be pure: no Date.now(), no await, no Firestore/firebase-admin import, no network — verified structurally by contract-f1 A6 (greps the function body for forbidden tokens), not just by these value fixtures.
